query_text: Allow more than one validator method to be registered for the same mapped attribute on a single class, so multiple independent validation routines can run when that attribute is set.
notes: Grounded by orm/mapper.py's validates() decorator (confirmed at line 4353). Distinct from 2943.rst, which concerns subclass-override behavior across a class hierarchy, not multiple validators on the same attribute within one class -- that specific capability was not confirmed to already exist.

query_text: Add a way to change an existing database sequence's configuration (such as its start value or increment) through the schema/DDL API, rather than only being able to create or drop a sequence entirely.
notes: Grounded by sql/ddl.py confirming CreateSequence (line 1077) and DropSequence (line 1083) exist, but no corresponding AlterSequence construct was found anywhere in ddl.py or compiler.py -- a confirmed, genuine gap. Replaces an earlier draft of this query (about PostgreSQL materialized view storage options) after a Phase 11 follow-up search found that feature already works: PGDDLCompiler.create_table_select_suffixes (dialects/postgresql/base.py:2824) applies postgresql_with for any CreateView regardless of its materialized flag, since visit_create_view always passes type_='view' (sql/compiler.py:7122-7123) irrespective of element.materialized.

query_text: Simplify the logic in the SQL compiler that decides which strategy to use when compiling an INSERT statement targeting multiple rows at once.
notes: Grounded by sql/compiler.py's confirmed _InsertManyValues/_InsertManyValuesBatch/InsertmanyvaluesSentinelOpts machinery.

query_text: Improve consistency across the built-in dialects in how each one implements reflection of database schema objects.
notes: Grounded by engine/reflection.py plus 13311.rst's own text noting that only some built-in dialects (PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server) were updated to use the new Inspector.has_multi_table method, implying a partial, cross-dialect inconsistency in reflection implementation -- framed generically as a refactor target, not asserting exactly which dialects still lag.

query_text: Investigate a test that behaves differently, or fails, depending on which database backend it is run against, and make it behave consistently across backends.
notes: Grounded by test/requirements.py, confirmed present at the top level of test/, which gates backend/dialect-specific test requirements -- implying tests are designed to run conditionally per backend. Resolved during the Phase 11 audit to concrete evidence in test/engine/test_reflection.py: line 1169 has `@testing.crashes("oracle", "FIXME: unknown, confirm not fails_on")` (a literal FIXME acknowledging unconfirmed backend-specific behavior) and line 2109 has `@testing.fails_on_everything_except("sqlite", "mysql", "mssql")` (a test confirmed to fail on all backends except three).
